tagline: Representational-geometry analysis of post-pruning recovery: why depth-pruned LLMs recover fluency but lose reasoning.
current_phase: Phase 25 causal interventions complete — NeurReps 2026 submission ready
phase_status: Phase 25 Causal Interventions: complete — manuscript audit-hardened and packaged for NeurReps 2026
research_question: Why does post-pruning recovery restore language-modeling fluency but leave multi-step reasoning collapsed — and is coordinated subspace rotation causally responsible for the dissociation?

overview.title: What we're building
overview.body: A depth pruning + Incision Boundary Healing pipeline (TIM-MGDT) and the causal representational-geometry analysis behind it. Boundary healing confines LoRA adaptation to the t layers flanking the incision site, recovering 4.04× more C4 perplexity gap than 6-layer global sensitivity LoRA with 33.3% fewer updates (Mistral-7B, Llama-3-8B; Gemma-2-2B needs t=3 due to sliding-window attention).

overview.title: Why this matters
overview.body: The central finding is the fluency–reasoning dissociation: healed models reach near-dense C4 PPL (9.12 vs 7.86) yet GSM8K collapses 39.6% → 1.8% → 6.2% (N=500, 8-shot CoT). Pruning induces a 33.93°–45.60° canonical subspace rotation plus PC₁ energy collapse; applying the pruning-derived inverse Procrustes rotation (R*)ᵀ to an intact model reproduces the collapse (39.6% → 9.0%, p = 5.6×10⁻³⁵), while planar controls leave accuracy intact (40.3%).

overview.title: Where we are today
overview.body: Phase 25 complete and audit-hardened. Every number in the NeurReps 2026 manuscript is backed 1:1 by JSON artifacts; the healed-geometry claim is a fresh paired measurement (Δθ = −1.90° ± 0.32°, Wilcoxon p ≈ 1.8×10⁻¹⁵); planar-control statistics use per-seed exact McNemar + Fisher combination (no cross-seed pooling); matched-angle controls at 34.02° and 28.71° across 3 seeds; inference-time repair attempts (Procrustes 1.8%, PC₁ un-rotation 1.6%) reported as negative controls. Main text ends on page 9; overleaf zip rebuilt.

decisions.rationale: LoRA adapters confined to the t layers flanking the cut recover 4.04× more perplexity gap than global sensitivity LoRA with 33.3% fewer parameter updates; Gemma-2-2B (SWA) requires t=3.
Boundary healing restores C4 PPL to near-dense (9.12 vs 7.86) while GSM8K recovers to only 6.2% (dense 39.6%, unhealed 1.8%) — fluency is not a proxy for reasoning.

All paired tests are two-tailed exact binomial McNemar; multi-seed conditions report per-seed p-values combined with Fisher's method. Cross-seed pooling is rejected as pseudo-replication (same 500 questions per seed). Geometry uses per-passage top-10 SVD angles with t-CIs over N=50 matched passages.

tasks.next_action: Fresh paired N=50 measurement on the boundary-healed adapter: θ 33.93° ± 0.77° (dropped) → 32.03° ± 0.76° (healed); Δθ = −1.90° ± 0.32°, Wilcoxon p ≈ 1.8×10⁻¹⁵. Replaced the unbacked Table 2 healed row.

Matched-angle controls re-run at 34.02° (3 seeds): 40.3% (39.8/40.6/40.4), per-seed p = 1.000/0.125/0.289, Fisher p = 0.36; 28.71° dose point 40.2%, Fisher p = 0.50. Union CIs [35.6, 45.0] / [35.8, 45.0].
Uniform per-passage protocol across all models: rotation curve k=1..4 = 20.24/25.41/29.74/34.02°; Llama 45.60°, Gemma 41.32°. Abstract/intro ranges updated to 33.93°–45.60°.
Procrustes R* realignment (1.8%) and PC₁ un-rotation (1.6%) added to Table 8: single-layer linear repair cannot undo multi-layer accumulation — training-time preservation required.

McNemar sentence matches code (exact binomial, clamped, no pooling); Appendix A discloses 1,000-vs-500 training budgets; per-passage SVD protocol stated after Eq. 4; single-seed dose angles marked; A100 → RTX 3090.
Table 1 footnote documents the Gemma dense LoRA-calibrated baseline (r=16, 1,000 C4 sequences, lr 1e-5; unmodified model = 63.89 under the same harness, re-verified 63.8894).
Manuscript is audit-hardened and packaged (`paper/neurreps2026_overleaf.zip`, 12 files). Submit before the NeurIPS 2026 workshop deadline.
